origin.description: Computes a weighted MAD of a numeric vector.
origin.usage:
weightedMad(x, w = NULL, idxs = NULL, na.rm = FALSE, constant = 1.4826,
  center = NULL, ...)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A vector of type integer, numeric, or logical.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: A vector of weights the same length as x giving the weights to use for each element of x. Negative weights are treated as zero weights. Default value is equal weight to all values.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A vector indicating subset of elements to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: constant
arguments.text: A numeric scale factor, cf. stats::mad.

arguments.name: center
arguments.text: Optional numeric scalar specifying the center location of the data. If NULL, it is estimated from data.

origin.details: Missing values are dropped at the very beginning, if argument na.rm is TRUE, otherwise not. For the non-weighted MAD, see stats::mad. Internally weightedMedian() is used to calculate the weighted median when w is not NULL. When w is NULL the function calls stats::median and stats::mad and does not apply idxs.

translation.description: Computes a weighted MAD of a numeric vector.
translation.usage:
weightedMad(x, w=None, idxs=None, na_rm=False, constant=1.4826,
  center=None, *, low=False, high=False)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: One-dimensional numeric vector, or a matrix read in column-major order. This is x in R.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: A vector of weights the same length as x. None calls stats::mad and ignores idxs. A weight of zero or less is dropped, including negative infinity, before a positive infinite weight is considered. A positive infinite weight then keeps only those observations, with equal weight. A missing weight makes the result missing even when na_rm is true, unless that observation was already dropped.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: 1-based vector indicating the subset of elements to operate over. None means no subsetting. Used only when w is given. Subsetting follows R's [ rules: zeros are dropped, negatives exclude, and a positive index past the end inserts a missing value.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values in x are dropped after non-positive weights. This is na.rm in R. The default is False, which returns a missing value when x still has one.

arguments.name: constant
arguments.text: Scale factor multiplied after the median of absolute deviations. The default is 1.4826, the same number stats::mad uses. When w is given it must be one numeric value. When w is None it is passed through to mad and may be a vector.

arguments.name: center
arguments.text: Optional numeric scalar. None estimates the center: stats::median when w is None, and weightedMedian when w is given. When w is given, a center that is not a single value is an error.

arguments.name: low
arguments.text: Passed to stats::mad when w is None. On an even count, return the lower of the two central absolute deviations instead of their mean. Ignored when w is given.

arguments.name: high
arguments.text: Passed to stats::mad when w is None. On an even count, return the upper of the two central absolute deviations. low and high together are an error only when that even-count branch runs.

translation.details: When w is None the result is stats::mad of x, including the default constant 1.4826, and idxs is not applied. When w is present, non-positive weights are removed first, missing values are then dropped or returned, and a positive infinite weight keeps only the infinite-weight observations. Zero observations return R's NA. One observation returns 0. Otherwise the center, unless one was supplied, and the median of the absolute deviations are weightedMedian, and that median is multiplied by constant.
translation.value: A numeric scalar. If no observation remains, the result is R's NA. A vector constant on the unweighted path returns one scaled value per element.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.weightedmad import weightedMad

x = np.arange(1, 11, dtype=float)
weightedMad(x)
